subject: Support crediting architecture and pilot terms — pricing options
messages:
From: Kevin Malik <kevin@heliocloud.com>

Subject: support crediting + pilot terms?

High level background: we expect a 3 month trial (roughly 4.5M tokens total) and if we convert want those to offset our first quarter usage. Also curious about how response-time SLA tiers (2h vs 4h) map to pricing and whether we can get a short-term uplift discount tied to TCV.

I attached a snapshot of last quarter's usage. Happy to hop on a call.

—Kevin

Thanks Kevin — appreciate the context and the file. Quick answers up front:
- We can structure pilot consumption to roll forward into committed credits if HelioCloud signs within the rollforward window (details below).
- SLA tiers are priced as add-on premium bands (standard: included; priority: +7.5% of hosted usage; enterprise fast lane 1: +15%). Response windows are 4h / 2h / 1h respectively.

I'll pull together 2 pragmatic commercial options: a short pilot conversion with partial rollforward and a committed-capacity offer that includes deeper discounts and guaranteed response coverage. I attached a draft worksheet with the math so you can play with volumes.

Would next Wednesday 10am PT work for a 30-minute review?

Best,

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding HelioCloud ask. Key asks: pilot rollforward into credits, mapping of SLA tiers to pricing uplift, and a potential short-term uplift discount tied to TCV.

Quoted below is Kevin's original note + the usage snapshot. I sketched two customer-favorable constructs in the worksheet but want your recommendation on: (1) what % of pilot should rollforward (0/50/70?), (2) whether to offer a time-limited uplift discount for conversion, and (3) which SLA band to push as the baseline for the committed offer.

Notes: Helio is an ISV with unpredictable bursty tokens but healthy long-term growth signal. Prior wins show that a partial rollforward (60–70%) materially helps conversion and still protects revenue. They asked explicitly for rollforward into Q1 credits.

Give me your take by EOD so I can finalize the external deck for tomorrow's review.

—Laura

Subject: Re: FW: support crediting + pilot terms? — suggested commercial options

Thanks for the context — my recommended constructs (numbers are illustrative, I used the worksheet):

Option 1 — Pilot -> Standard Conversion (Conservative)
- Pilot: 3 months, no rollforward (pilot consumed).
- Conversion: immediate start of committed plan with standard committed discounts (5% for 12-month commit, 8% for 24-month).
- SLA: baseline 4h included; priority lane add-on +7.5% billed net.
- Rationale: minimal revenue risk, clean accounting.

Option 2 — Pilot Rollforward (Conversion Incentive) [Recommended]
- Pilot: 3 months. If customer signs within 30 days of pilot end, up to 70% of pilot usage can be credited against the first full quarter of committed usage (rollforward cap = vendor discretion; here 70%).
- Conversion: 12-month commit recommended. Apply accelerated TCV uplift discount (one-time 10% on committed host invoicing for first 3 months) to offset conversion friction.
- SLA: include priority lane (2h response) for first 6 months at no additional uplift, then reverts to +7.5% thereafter.
- Rationale: eases procurement, increases likelihood to convert, limited revenue impact if capped.

Option 3 — Committed Capacity (Aggressive discount)
- Commit: 12–24 months with minimum monthly commit (equivalent to 6M tokens/month). Discount: 12% on hosted usage, includes enterprise fast lane (1h).
- Rollforward: N/A for pilot, but offer service credits for missed SLAs.
- Rationale: protects unit economics and gives better unit price.

TCV impact: Option 2 reduces near-term gross revenue but increases conversion velocity — modeled ~+40% probability of conversion vs Option 1. Option 3 yields lowest unit price but requires procurement appetite.

Concession guidance: if legal wants a firm cap on rollforward exposure, tie rollforward credit to a monetary cap equal to 70% of pilot consumption or $X (whichever lower).

Happy to join the call and frame this to Helio — I lean Option 2 as the best win probability vs revenue tradeoff.

—Karthik
Director, Pricing & Commercial Ops

Attachment referenced: support-crediting-worksheet.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-13T16:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: support crediting + pilot terms? — proposed options and next steps

Kevin — thanks for the patience. Based on internal alignment (pricing & product), here are three clean paths you can choose from. Full worksheet attached and I pasted the essentials below so it's easy to compare.

Option A — Convert-as-you-go (Conservative)
- 3-month pilot (no rollforward).
- Default: 4h response SLA included.
- Standard committed pricing if you sign for 12 months: 5% off hosted rates.
- Good if procurement prefers clean P&L.

Option B — Pilot Rollforward (Recommended)
- 3-month pilot. If you sign within 30 days of pilot completion we will credit up to 70% of pilot consumption as a prepayment against your first quarter of committed usage (rollforward monetary cap: $60k).
- As a conversion incentive we will apply a one-time 10% TCV uplift credit (applied across first billing cycle) if you commit 12 months.
- Priority 2h response lane included free for first 6 months; then +7.5% uplift thereafter.
- This preserves revenue while materially improving conversion probability.

Option C — Committed Capacity (Deep discount)
- 12-month commit at higher monthly baseline (min 6M tokens/mo).
- 12% off hosted usage, includes 1h enterprise lane.
- No pilot rollforward but SLA credits and a dedicated onboarding window.

Next steps
- If you want to proceed with Option B I can send a short SOW + DocuSign that captures the rollforward cap and the 30-day election window.
- Otherwise we can take Option A and start the conversion conversation once the pilot completes.

Proposed call to align commercial terms: Thursday 8/20 10am PT — is that good for you?

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
